title: Genome-Wide CRISPR Screens Identify Multiple Synthetic Lethal Targets That Enhance KRAS(G12C) Inhibitor Efficacy
model: Four KRAS-G12C NSCLC lines (H2030, H2122, H23, HCC44), genome-wide knockout library, MRTX849 +/- TNO155
contrast: MRTX849 vs DMSO, 8 doublings, pooled over 4 cell lines (8 vs 8); COMBO vs DMSO also analyzed
paper_method: MAGeCK (synthetic-lethal screen; paper not open access)
paper_calls: Hippo-pathway genes enriched among MRTX hits, motivating a KRAS-G12C + TEAD inhibitor combination
barcs_calls: 25 genes at FDR 0.10 in the MRTX screen (calibrated to controls); 1,882 in the far more cytotoxic COMBO screen
named_hits: NF2 #1, KIRREL #2, LATS2 #3, NRP1 #4, TAOK1 #5, AMOTL2 #7 (all resistance, FDR 0.10); WWTR1/TAZ depleted #11
verdict: BARCS places the paper's Hippo-pathway resistance genes (NF2, KIRREL, LATS2, TAOK1) at the very top of the MRTX screen, all FDR-significant, reproducing the finding that motivates the G12C + TEAD inhibitor combination.
